introduction:
GLRMask is a grammar-constrained decoding library for high-throughput LLM serving. It is optimized for fast mask computation with extremely low tail latency, even for complex grammars.

GLRMask supports general context-free grammars, including ambiguous ones. It accepts GLRM (its native grammar format), JSON Schema, and Lark.
usage:
GLRMask has four core types:

- `Grammar`: the source-language definition, without compilation settings.
- `Module`: a reusable, independently configured grammar with bindings and any retained compilation work. It may still have unresolved externs.
- `Constraint`: a fully runnable grammar compiled against a specific vocabulary.
- `ConstraintState`: the mutable state for a single generated sequence.

Use direct `Grammar.compile` for a closed source, or a `Module` when local
settings, late-bound children, or retained work are needed. `Expr.choice` and
`Expr.sequence` group grammar leaves without adding an extra lexer scope at each
operator. See [modules and expressions](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/docs/module-api.md)
for construction, open precompilation, and persistence examples.

quickstarts.python:
```python
import glrmask

vocab = glrmask.Vocab.from_id_to_bytes({0: b"hello", 1: b" ", 2: b"world"})
grammar = glrmask.Grammar.from_ebnf('start ::= "hello" " " "world"')
constraint = grammar.compile(vocab)
state = constraint.start()
for token_id, expected in [(0, [True, False, False]),
                           (1, [False, True, False]),
                           (2, [False, False, True])]:
    assert state.mask().tolist() == expected
    state.commit_token(token_id)
assert state.is_accepting()
```

Python masks are NumPy Boolean arrays indexed by original model token ID.

The next compatibility release targets ordinary, GIL-enabled CPython 3.9
through 3.15. Its `cp39-abi3` wheels use Python's stable extension ABI, so one
wheel per operating-system/architecture combination can serve multiple Python
versions. This does not imply support for free-threaded Python (`cp314t`,
`cp315t` or `abi3t`): the extension explicitly retains the GIL requirement.

The expanded build matrix covers Windows x64/ARM64, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon,
and Linux x64/ARM64 with either glibc or musl. Linux glibc Python wheels retain
the manylinux2014 baseline; native C++/Node binaries use glibc 2.28 or newer.
See [the compatibility guide](https://github.com/IsaacBreen/glrmask/blob/main/docs/compatibility.md)
for runtime requirements and the distinction between source support and
published package availability.

python_symbols.MaskStrategy: Mask generation strategy: trade off compilation time against per-token masking latency.
python_symbols.MaskStrategy.PARSER_DWA: Static parser-DWA masks (slowest build, fastest masks).
python_symbols.MaskStrategy.TOKEN_CLASS_TRIE: Token-trie walk over token equivalence classes.
python_symbols.BoundaryMaskStrategy: Boundary mask detail level: minimum metadata to build for composition boundaries.
python_symbols.BoundaryMaskStrategy.FAST_RUNTIME: Full exact proper-prefix boundary trigger (lower latency).
python_symbols.Token: An original token ID with no vocabulary identity. Only ID membership is checked against the target vocabulary; the same ID can refer to different bytes. Use `vocab.tokens([id])` for a vocabulary-bound singleton.
python_symbols.ExactTokens: One token event chosen from a vocabulary-bound set. Vocabularies must have the same ID-to-byte mapping and exact-only IDs, even for a singleton. An empty set matches nothing.
python_symbols.ExactTokens.ids: Sorted IDs, materialized on access. Prefer `ranges` for large sets.
python_symbols.ExactTokens.ranges: Normalized, disjoint Python ranges with exclusive stops; does not expand the IDs.
python_symbols.ExactTokens.__len__: Number of IDs, rather than ranges.
python_symbols.Vocab: Original model IDs mapped to exact token bytes. IDs may be sparse; masks keep their original positions. Reuse one vocabulary across components to share compilation caches.
python_symbols.Vocab.from_dict: String keys are UTF-8 encoded; byte keys are used verbatim. IDs must fit an unsigned 32-bit integer.
python_symbols.Vocab.from_id_to_bytes: Use the tokenizer’s exact decoded bytes, including partial UTF-8 sequences, rather than display spellings.
python_symbols.Vocab.from_llama_cpp: Extract the byte vocabulary from a llama-cpp-python `Llama`. EOG, control, unused and empty-piece tokens are omitted from byte matching; use `llama_cpp_end_token_ids` for the root stopping policy.
python_symbols.Vocab.llama_cpp_end_token_ids: EOG IDs discovered by `from_llama_cpp`; pass them as `end_tokens` when compiling.
python_symbols.Vocab.tokens: Match one of the supplied IDs. Unknown or duplicate IDs are errors; empty input matches nothing. The result retains vocabulary identity, including for a singleton. Contiguous ranges remain compact; other iterables are consumed once.
python_symbols.Vocab.token_ranges: Union of nonempty Python ranges with step 1 or -1 and exclusive stops. Overlapping or adjacent ranges merge; unknown IDs are errors. Empty input matches nothing. Use `tokens` for arbitrary strides.
python_symbols.Vocab.__len__: Counts byte-backed entries; exact-only control IDs are excluded.
python_symbols.Extern: One declared extern contract on a Module.
python_symbols.Extern.name: Declared extern name.
python_symbols.Extern.kind: A token extern accepts exact events; a grammar extern accepts grammar/module/expr components.
python_symbols.Extern.span: `(start_byte, end_byte, line, column)` in the declaring source, or `None`. The byte interval is half-open; line and Unicode-scalar column are one-based.
python_symbols.Externs: Read-only snapshot view of a Module's declared externs. Implements collections.abc.Mapping.
python_symbols.Externs.unbound: Filtered view containing only externs not yet bound.
python_symbols.Expr: Immutable scope-preserving union, concatenation, or byte-literal leaves.
python_symbols.Expr.choice: Unordered context-free union. Empty choice matches nothing. Open parts raise ValueError immediately.
python_symbols.Expr.sequence: Concatenation of language pieces. Empty sequence matches epsilon. Open parts raise ValueError immediately.
python_symbols.Expr.literal: Match exact bytes without whitespace or ignore inserted (str is UTF-8 encoded).
python_symbols.Module: An owned, independently configured reusable grammar with snapshot-safe mutable bindings and retained compilation work.
python_symbols.Module.__init__: Create a cold module from a Grammar with settings.
python_symbols.Module.mask_strategy: Mask generation strategy for this module.
python_symbols.Module.boundary_mask_strategy: Boundary mask detail level for this module.
python_symbols.Module.bind: Fill one extern. Each extern can be bound once; names containing `::` are rejected.
python_symbols.Module.precompile: Perform and retain definition-local work for this vocabulary even while externs are open. Existing clones are unchanged.
python_symbols.Module.compile: Create a runnable constraint. Requires all externs resolved.
python_symbols.Module.externs: Read-only snapshot mapping of this module's own declared externs in declaration order.
python_symbols.Module.copy: Return an independent snapshot sharing immutable source and retained work.
python_symbols.Module.save: Serialize source, settings, bindings and retained work without compiling.
python_symbols.Module.load: Load a saved module artifact, restoring settings and retained work.
python_symbols.Grammar: Immutable authored source grammar without compilation settings or bindings.
python_symbols.Grammar.from_ebnf: Parsing and compilation errors can be deferred until `compile`.
python_symbols.Grammar.from_glrm: GLRM supports typed external declarations; bind them via `Module(g).bind(...)` before compiling.
python_symbols.Grammar.from_json_schema: Accepts JSON text or a JSON-serializable object.
python_symbols.Grammar.from_lark: The default `recognition` profile and the `llm` extension profile differ in accepted syntax.
python_symbols.Grammar.compile: Compile this grammar directly. Sugar for `Module(self, ...).compile(vocab, end_tokens=...)`.
python_symbols.Constraint: Immutable runnable grammar and root stopping policy. Reuse across sequences; each `start` creates independent mutable state.
python_symbols.Constraint.marker_ids: Sorted, distinct application marker IDs, independent of model token IDs.
python_symbols.Constraint.mask_len: Packed 32-bit word count for `fill_mask`, not the Boolean-array length returned by `mask`.
python_symbols.Constraint.save: Embeds the vocabulary by default. With `external_vocab=True`, loading requires the exact original token-ID/byte mapping, not merely the same vocabulary size.
python_symbols.Constraint.load: Rejects malformed or incompatible artifacts. Supply `vocab` for external-vocabulary artifacts; it must match the original mapping.
python_symbols.ConstraintState: Mutable state for one generated sequence.
python_symbols.ConstraintState.clone: Independent snapshot at the current prefix.
python_symbols.ConstraintState.mask: New Boolean array indexed by original token ID.
python_symbols.ConstraintState.fill_mask: Fill a contiguous, writable 1-D NumPy `int32` array with at least `Constraint.mask_len()` words.
python_symbols.ConstraintState.commit_token: Advance by a token event. Unknown or forbidden IDs reject the state.
python_symbols.ConstraintState.commit_bytes: Advance by raw bytes rather than model token events.
python_symbols.ConstraintState.is_accepting: The current prefix is a complete grammar match.
python_symbols.ConstraintState.is_rejected: The prefix cannot be extended to a valid match.
python_symbols.ConstraintState.forced_tokens: Read-only canonical prefix of forced tokens.
python_symbols.ConstraintState.marker_events: Initial or most recent commit’s `(marker_id, absolute_byte_offset)` batch, sorted by offset then ID.
python_symbols.auto: Adaptive JSON Schema policy inspection and persisted tier selection. For ordinary compilation, prefer `Grammar.compile(..., mask_strategy=MaskStrategy.AUTO)`. Policy thresholds are empirical choices, not latency guarantees. All tiers inherit the JSON Schema importer’s partial assertion support.
python_symbols.auto.AutoSchemaShape: Source-shape counts used by the policy, not a schema validation result. `json_bytes` measures normalized JSON serialized with sorted keys and compact separators.
python_symbols.auto.json_schema_auto_shape: Extract the policy’s source-shape features from JSON text or a JSON-serializable schema.
python_symbols.auto.select_json_schema_auto_tier: Select `o1`, `o2` or `o3` using fitted source-shape thresholds. The choice predicts a compilation/masking trade-off; it does not guarantee a latency bound.
python_symbols.auto.AutoConstraint: Constraint wrapper that records the selected tier and policy. Its artifact carries the tier so loading does not rerun selection. JSON Schema assertions unsupported by the importer may remain unenforced.
python_symbols.auto.AutoConstraint.__init__: Use `from_json_schema` for normal construction; unknown tier names raise `ValueError`.
python_symbols.auto.AutoConstraint.from_json_schema: Choose a tier and compile. Accepts schema text or an object; inherits the importer’s partial JSON Schema support.
python_symbols.auto.AutoConstraint.load: Restore the recorded tier. Rejects missing or unknown artifact tags; the supplied vocabulary must match the original.
python_symbols.auto.AutoConstraint.save: Includes the tier tag and underlying constraint artifact.
python_symbols.auto.AutoConstraint.start: Independent decoding state with the same mask/commit interface as `ConstraintState`.
python_symbols.auto.AutoConstraint.mask_len: Packed 32-bit word count for a mask buffer.
